# ADR-0019: Admission ledger for external inputs

> **Status:** accepted | **Date:** 2026-08-04

**References:** [ADR-0003](../adr/ADR-0003.md), [ADR-0018](../adr/ADR-0018.md), [RFC-0001](../rfc/RFC-0001.md)

## Context

Every external input was volatile, unrecorded, or both. Steer text was lost on pod death after read-then-blank. Approve/deny/rescope were in-memory mutex slots (double approve, silent overwrite, lost on pod death). Set-budget/pause reverted on resume. No idempotency keys existed.

## Decision

Append-only NDJSON file (state/admissions.jsonl) with a two-state machine per idempotency key: exactly one "admitted", then at most one "settled". Adapted from flue's AgentSubmissionStore. Three rules: admission precedes effect (fsync before mutation), idempotency converges (same key+payload returns original), ledger is authoritative for operator inputs. Derived grant keys link approvals to asks. Settlement is keyed to turn completion. File mechanics live in forge::ndjson (flock-guarded append, torn-tail-tolerant fold).

## Consequences

The control bridge no longer writes STEER.md. Two durable logs can disagree after a crash (one declared authoritative). Each admission costs an fsync. The file is never compacted.

## Alternatives Considered

### Append-only NDJSON ledger with two-state machine per idempotency key (accepted)


### In-memory mutex slots with checkpoint snapshots to disk (rejected)

- **Rejected because:** Snapshots are point-in-time and lose inputs between checkpoints. The append-only ledger records every admission with fsync-before-effect, so no input is lost on crash.
